text.tspan: Data preparation begins by taking a reference frame to locate the initial hand and object bounding boxes.
The object within the reference frame is isolated and replaced to serve as the target object.
The source video provides input frames capturing human motion and interaction with the object.
Bounding box detection defines spatial layouts, while hand mesh augmentation applies random
position shifts to decouple pose from fixed locations.
In the training pipeline, the reference image supplies the visual appearance context of the target object.
A frozen VAE encoder encodes this image, while the Reference U-Net extracts multi-scale
appearance features across self-attention layers.
Sequences of reconstructed hand meshes are processed by ControlNet to inject accurate hand pose
and structural cues.
Layout guidance is encoded through a lightweight layout encoder and combined with Gaussian noise
to initialize the diffusion latent.
The Denoising U-Net integrates reference self-attention, ControlNet features, specialized hand
and object attention, and temporal attention layers.
The denoised latent is decoded by the VAE decoder to reconstruct temporally coherent
reenacted video frames.
The Hand-Object Interaction Restoration Module refines fine-grained details through dedicated
hand and object memory banks.
In Hand Attention, ControlNet queries perform cross-attention with a Hand Texture Memory Bank
under the guidance of a hand mask.
Similarly, Object Attention queries an Object Texture Memory Bank guided by an object mask
to restore sharp, realistic object textures.
